title: Security in Depth: KMS, Secrets, and Encryption

options.text: Layering multiple independent controls so that if one fails, others still protect you
Relying on a single strong firewall

questions.explanation: Defense in depth layers network, identity, data, and detection controls so a single failure isn't catastrophic.

questions.prompt: Why is encrypting data at rest not sufficient on its own?

options.text: It also encrypts data in transit automatically
It protects stored data but not data moving over the network, which needs TLS/HTTPS

questions.explanation: At-rest and in-transit encryption are separate protections. Data on disk can be encrypted while it's still exposed on the wire without TLS — you need both.

questions.prompt: In AWS KMS envelope encryption, what happens to the plaintext key material?

options.text: It never leaves KMS; KMS encrypts/decrypts data keys and logs every use
It is stored in the S3 object's metadata
It is printed in CloudWatch logs

questions.explanation: With envelope encryption, data is encrypted by a data key that KMS itself encrypts; the plaintext KMS key material never leaves KMS, and CloudTrail records every use.

questions.prompt: What is the advantage of AWS Secrets Manager over hardcoding a database password?

options.text: It stores the secret outside code, serves it at runtime via IAM, and can rotate it automatically
It makes the password public for convenience

questions.explanation: Secrets Manager keeps the secret out of the repo, delivers it at runtime through IAM, and can rotate it on a schedule so a copied credential soon expires.

questions.prompt: Match each detection/protection service to its purpose.
questions.explanation: GuardDuty detects threats, WAF is a web application firewall, Shield defends against DDoS, and Macie finds sensitive data in S3.

questions.prompt: Data moving over the network should be protected in transit using ____ (the common encryption protocol for the web).
questions.explanation: TLS (used by HTTPS) encrypts data in transit; pair it with encryption at rest for end-to-end protection.
